Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital payment systems.  21 variables in 4 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether the instant payment system enables or plans to enable instant payments across national borders to other countries or regional payment systems, supporting remittances, trade, and regional integration.
Comments: No evidence found of Somalia participating in PAPSS or having live cross-border instant payment linkages; UNCDF 2023 assessment notes Somalia's large-value payment system (RTGS/ACH) did not participate in regional/international payment platforms as of March 2022 and cross-border relies on bilateral arrangements via banks.
revision_notes: Fetched the cited 2023 UNCDF report, which confirms the original 'No' finding was accurate for its time (Somalia's RTGS/ACH not connected to any regional platform as of March 2022). However this is now stale: the Central Bank of Somalia (CBS) announced in an official statement (via the Somali Bankers Association and Dawan Africa, both dated March/April 2026) that it has officially joined PAPSS. A CBS LinkedIn statement confirms it signed the PAPSS Membership Agreement in March 2026 and has since been working with PAPSS on onboarding and integration. PAPSS's own network coverage documents (April and June 2026) still list Somalia as 'upcoming'/'live soon' rather than live, with two banks (East African Bank, Salaam African Bank) named as being onboarded. Somalia is therefore not yet a live/functional PAPSS participant, ruling out 4 or 5, but active technical integration work is underway, which is more than merely 'planned'. Recalculated from 1 (No) to 3 (Under development). Not flagged for human review as this is a mid-scale, well-evidenced change from multiple corroborating primary/authoritative sources (CBS-affiliated statements and PAPSS's own coverage documentation), not a top-of-scale promotion.
revised_comments: The Central Bank of Somalia signed the PAPSS Membership Agreement in March 2026 and is currently undertaking technical onboarding and integration with the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System. Two Somali banks, East African Bank and Salaam African Bank, are named in PAPSS's network coverage documentation as being onboarded, with Somalia listed as 'live soon' rather than live as of June 2026. Cross-border instant payment functionality is therefore under development but not yet operational.
